author: ojiudezue
title: v5.103.66 shipped: Reserve write governor: one floor, truthful reserve_write rows, bypass lint, optimizer reserve deny
summary: Reserve write governor: one floor, truthful reserve_write rows, bypass lint, optimizer reserve deny
why: Governor first, before inclement hardening: three inclement plan reviews (5/9/6 HIGHs) kept finding floor leaks because the floor was applied per branch across ~25 branches. Fixing branches one by one was whack-a-mole, so we centralised the floor at _result and made writes observable instead of adding more per-branch clamps. Rejected: a new writer class (operator pointed at HVAC WriteStatus/preset writer as prior art; reused WriteStatus and the existing wv_commanded_ledger instead of new persistence). Review D found the optimizer could write the reserve via variable-domain services with no row (not live, OC in shadow); operator chose to keep the hard deny in-cycle. Review C found 8 untested sites; all now mutation-anchored. Built on Fable 5.1.
implications: Shipped EC-RESERVE-WRITE-GOVERNOR-1 at v5.103.66; card(s) sit shipped_organic pending validation. Acceptance in README_v5.103.66.md (Live criteria).
revisit_trigger: ura_activity_log has >=1 reserve_write row with non-null value/path/status per day of reserve changes, and count(reserve_write rows) within ~2x of number.iq_battery_hacs_battery_reserve state changes over 24h

refs.release_notes: Arc step 1 of EC resilience. The battery reserve was written from ~25 branches with little record and floor leaks kept recurring. Now: a single inclement floor at _result, a reserve_write activity row at each real dispatch point (WriteStatus vocabulary, change-gated, FAILED never arms the gate), an AST lint pinning every reserve set_value writer, and an optimizer hard deny on the reserve entities. Decisions are byte-identical (A/B golden). Tier 3: 4 reviews, all fixes mutation-drilled.
